expectations.evidence: 'Committee: multi-tier cascade'

expectations.text: Describes track committees scoring within their own track as the first tier
expectations.evidence: 'They score only their own track.'

expectations.text: States that the top-scoring 30% advance from track committees to track chairs
expectations.evidence: 'The top 30% per track advance to track chairs: 630 proposals'

expectations.text: States that track chairs pass roughly 30% of those on - about 9% of the original pool - to the co-chairs
expectations.evidence: 'Chairs pass ~30%... ~189 in total (9% of the pool).'

expectations.text: States that comments are mandatory when track chairs pass proposals up to the co-chairs

expectations.text: Places the final accept decision with the co-chairs, combining committee scores with a program-fit overlay

expectations.text: Recommends the multi-criteria star scale across content, originality, relevance and speaker fit, with mandatory written feedback on every rating, because these reviewers will not all meet

expectations.text: Rejects the 26.4% academic figure as non-transferable, explaining that a peer-reviewed venue accepts what clears a quality bar while a conference fills a fixed number of slots in a room
expectations.evidence: 'Academic venues accept what clears a quality bar. A conference fills a fixed number of slots in a room.'

expectations.text: Treats the resulting acceptance ratio of roughly 96 in 2,100 as an outcome to record rather than a target to hit
expectations.evidence: 'Treat the ratio as a record, not a target.'

expectations.text: Cites a developer-conference calibration point such as PyCon US 2025 selecting about 15% of 938 proposals or KubeCon EU 2024 accepting 9% of 2,541

expectations.text: States that no published reviewers-per-proposal curve exists, and labels any per-proposal reviewer count it proposes as an interpolation
